title: Restore the rb and rtc elements and update ruby content model accordingly

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

labels.name: do not merge yet
labels.description: Pull request must not be merged per rationale in comment

body:
This pull request un-obsoletes the rb and rtc elements, changes the content model to take them into account, and updates the rendering section accordingly. It does not make any changes to parsing. As discussed in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1771, the ruby model currently defined in the HTML spec isn't quite enough to support the needs of ruby. The additional `rb` and `rtc` elements are needed to properly express the full semantics that need to be there for styling and fallback to work properly. See explanation in [fantasai’s blog post](http://fantasai.inkedblade.net/weblog/2011/ruby/) (which the [CSS Ruby Layout spec](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-ruby-1/) and the proposed markup model are both based on) and in the proposed specification text itself. The model defined here is the same one that had been defined in the old W3C HTML5 specification. The pull request contains two commits: one that imports the W3C spec text, and one that substantially reworks the prose and examples to better explain its semantics. We recommend reviewing the combined result; the commit split is largely to preserve history. - [ ] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * This model is the one currently implemented by Firefox * Chrome [has expressed support for unobsoleting rb and rtc](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/121#issuecomment-246178606) and [intends to work on this](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1771#issuecomment-534118162) * Amazon Kindle's ePub implementation [supports](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1771#issuecomment-797769743) `rb` as defined in this pull request - [ ] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/28017 * More tests exist about this that aren't directly about HTML: the CSS-RUBY spec assumes this model, and also has tests already in wpt: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/tree/master/css/css-ruby * a few existing HTML tests already use css from the CSS-RUBY spec, which assumes this model (e.g. `grep -RI "ruby-.*-container" wpt/html | wc -w` yields 67) * The `html5lib_*` tests under https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/tree/master/html/syntax/parsing should be updated as well, but they are autogenerated from https://github.com/html5lib/html5lib-python/. probably, the best course of action is to land this PR, then update html5lib accordingly, then update wpt. - [ ] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chrome: parsing already implemented (since it's not changed), various bugs filed against CSS support (e.g. [27569](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=27659)) * Firefox: parsing and CSS support already implemented * Safari: parsing already implemented (since it's not changed), differences detectable through support of css, for which there are [many bugs filed](https://bugs.webkit.org/buglist.cgi?quicksearch=ruby) CC @r12a @kojiishii @upsuper *** ### :boom: Error: 503 Service Unavailable :boom: ### [PR Preview](https://github.com/tobie/pr-preview#pr-preview) failed to build. _(Last tried on Oct 6, 2021, 12:47 AM UTC)_.
